Accessibility

Accessibility

Altiora should work for everyone, including people who use a keyboard, a screen reader, zoom or a small screen. This page says what has been done, what is still limited, and how to tell us about a problem.

Last updated 14 November 2026

What we have done

  • Automated checks. We test the home page, the app (home, check and shortlist views), a field guide and these information pages with axe-core against the WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA rules, at desktop and phone widths, with every expandable panel both open and closed. The most recent check found no violations.
  • Contrast. Text colours are checked for contrast against WCAG AA as part of those automated checks.
  • Text size. No text on the checked pages is smaller than 12px.
  • Small screens. The checked pages fit a 375px-wide screen without sideways scrolling.
  • Keyboard. Every link, button and form control can be reached and used with the keyboard, and shows a clear outline when it has focus. We have tested the About panel, the subject picker, the grade selectors and the Entry requirements panels by keyboard.
  • Screen readers. Decorative icons are hidden from screen readers. Course statuses are always written out in words, never shown by colour or icon alone.
  • Motion. If your device is set to reduce motion, animations are switched off.

Known limitations

  • Automated tools cannot find every problem, and we have not yet tested the site with a full range of screen readers and browsers.
  • Requirement text is taken from universities’ own pages, so it can include their abbreviations and wording.
  • The university websites we link to are outside our control and may not meet the same standard.

Report a problem

If something on Altiora is hard to use or doesn’t work with your device or assistive technology, email support@usealtiora.com. Tell us which page you were on and what happened, and we will look into it.
